scope: Open review of diffuse alveolar haemorrhage with emphasis on SLE, including the capillaritis versus bland histologic split and the rapid onset of haemoptysis.

keyRecommendations.text: DAH has a capillaritis phenotype and a bland non-inflammatory phenotype.
Haemoptysis can develop over hours or a few days. ANCA vasculitis and antiphospholipid syndrome are other groups at risk.
Risk is higher in active lupus nephritis.

clinicalBottomLine: Treat suspected DAH as a rapidly evolving pulmonary haemorrhage syndrome that may be capillaritis or bland haemorrhage, and look for SLE, ANCA vasculitis, and antiphospholipid syndrome.
notableCaveats: The review is centred on SLE. It is used because it states the general histologic split and the clinical tempo of DAH.

source.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, etiology and novel treatment strategies.
